sorular.soru: How many articles of faith are there?
sorular.aciklama: There are six articles of faith: belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, both good and bad.

sorular.soru: According to the hadith of Jibril, which of the following is NOT among the articles of faith?
sorular.aciklama: The hadith of Jibril is the hadith in which Jibril, peace be upon him, came in human form and asked about Islam, iman, and ihsan. Sawm is one of the five pillars of Islam; it is not one of the six articles of faith.

sorular.soru: What does belief in tawhid (the oneness of Allah) mean?
secenekler: A) That there are two Allahs
B) That Allah is One and Unique
D) That there is more than one deity
sorular.aciklama: Tawhid is believing that Allah is One and Unique, without partner or equal. It is the fundamental principle of iman.

sorular.soru: What is the first verse of Surah al-Ikhlas?
secenekler: A) "Allah is the Most Merciful and the Most Compassionate"
B) "Say: He is Allah, the One and Unique"
C) "There is no deity but Allah"
D) "Allah has power over all things"
sorular.aciklama: The first verse of Surah al-Ikhlas is: "Say: He is Allah, the One and Unique." (al-Ikhlas 112/1) It is a concise expression of belief in tawhid.

sorular.soru: What does the word "Samed" in Surah al-Ikhlas mean?
secenekler: C) The One whom everything needs and who needs nothing
D) The One with infinite power
sorular.aciklama: Samed means the One whom every being needs and who Himself needs nothing. (al-Ikhlas 112/2)

sorular.soru: In which surah do the words "He neither begets nor was He begotten. Nothing is equal to Him" appear?
sorular.aciklama: These are the third and fourth verses of Surah al-Ikhlas. They declare Allah's uniqueness and that He is free from deficiencies such as being born or giving birth.

sorular.soru: In which sources is the hadith of Jibril narrated?
sorular.aciklama: The hadith of Jibril is narrated in both Bukhari (Iman 37) and Muslim (Iman 1). This hadith, which defines Islam, iman, and ihsan, is among the fundamental sources.

sorular.soru: What does it mean that Allah is eternal, without beginning or end?
secenekler: A) He has a beginning but no end
B) He has no beginning but has an end
C) He has neither beginning nor end
D) He is limited by time
sorular.aciklama: Allah is eternal, without beginning or end. He is not limited by time or space; while everything needs Him, He needs nothing.

sorular.soru: What were angels created from?
sorular.aciklama: Angels were created from light. They do not sin and obey Allah's commands without fail.

sorular.soru: Which angel is tasked with bringing revelation to the prophets?
sorular.aciklama: Jibril, peace be upon him, is the great angel tasked with conveying Allah's revelation (divine knowledge from Allah) to the prophets. He is also referred to in the Quran as "Ruh al-Qudus" (the holy or pure spirit) and "Ruh al-Amin" (the trustworthy spirit).

sorular.soru: Which angel is tasked with taking souls?
sorular.aciklama: Azrail, peace be upon him, is tasked with taking souls; he is also known as Malak al-Mawt (the angel of death).

sorular.soru: What is Mikail's duty?
secenekler: D) To govern rain and natural events
sorular.aciklama: Mikail, peace be upon him, is the great angel tasked with governing rain, wind, and natural events.

sorular.soru: When will Israfil blow the trumpet?
secenekler: B) At the end of the world and at the resurrection
sorular.aciklama: Israfil, peace be upon him, will blow the trumpet first to bring about the end of the world and a second time for the resurrection of humanity.

sorular.soru: What do the angels Kiramen Katibin (the noble recorders) do?
secenekler: D) Question people in the grave
sorular.aciklama: Kiramen Katibin (the noble recorders) are the angels who are on each person's right and left, recording their deeds (their good and bad actions).

sorular.soru: What is the duty of Munker and Nakir?
secenekler: C) To conduct the questioning in the grave
sorular.aciklama: Munker and Nakir are the angels tasked with questioning people in the grave. This questioning is described as taking place during the life of barzakh after death.

sorular.soru: Which statement about angels is FALSE?
secenekler: A) They were created from light
C) They can take any form
D) They obey Allah's commands without fail
sorular.aciklama: Angels do not sin; this is their most fundamental characteristic. The remaining options correctly describe angels.

sorular.soru: To which prophet was the Torah revealed?
sorular.aciklama: The Torah is the great divine book revealed to Prophet Musa.

sorular.soru: To which prophet was the Zabur revealed?
sorular.aciklama: The Zabur is the great divine book revealed to Prophet Dawud.

sorular.soru: To which prophet was the Injil revealed?
sorular.aciklama: The Injil is the great divine book revealed to Prophet Isa.

sorular.soru: What are the four great divine books?
secenekler: A) The Torah, Zabur, Injil, and Quran
B) The Torah, Injil, Quran, and Suhuf
C) The Zabur, Injil, Quran, and scrolls
D) The Torah, Zabur, Injil, and hadith
sorular.aciklama: The four great divine books are the Torah (Prophet Musa), the Zabur (Prophet Dawud), the Injil (Prophet Isa), and the Noble Quran (Prophet Muhammad ﷺ).

sorular.soru: What are the Suhuf (divine scrolls)?
secenekler: B) Short scrolls of revelation given to certain prophets
D) Books of Quranic commentary written later
sorular.aciklama: The Suhuf are short scrolls of revelation given to certain prophets. The word means scrolls, that is, divine pages.

sorular.soru: How many scrolls were revealed to Prophet Ibrahim?
sorular.aciklama: Ten scrolls were revealed to Prophet Ibrahim.

sorular.soru: How many scrolls were revealed to Prophet Shith?
sorular.aciklama: Fifty scrolls were revealed to Prophet Shith.

sorular.soru: Which of the following is NOT among the prophets who received scrolls (suhuf)?
sorular.aciklama: The great book called the Zabur was revealed to Prophet Dawud. Common Islamic catechism teaching identifies Prophet Adam, Prophet Shith, Prophet Idris, and Prophet Ibrahim as recipients of suhuf.

sorular.soru: Who was the first prophet?
sorular.aciklama: The first of the prophets is Adam (peace be upon him). He is the first of both humanity and the line of prophets.

sorular.soru: Who is the last of the prophets?
sorular.aciklama: Muhammad ﷺ is the last of the prophets. "Khatam an-Nabiyyin" means the seal of the prophets, that is, the last prophet. (al-Ahzab 33:40)

sorular.soru: What is the fundamental principle of belief in the prophets?
secenekler: A) Belief in Muhammad (peace be upon him) alone is sufficient
B) No distinction is made between them; one must believe in all of them
C) One believes only in those named in the Quran
D) Belief in the prophet of one's own time is sufficient
sorular.aciklama: A Muslim believes in all the prophets sent by Allah. Knowingly rejecting one of the prophets is a serious matter for one's iman.

sorular.soru: What does rasul mean?
secenekler: A) A person who receives inspiration only
B) A prophet given a new law or a special mission to convey a message
C) A scholar who is a close servant of Allah
sorular.aciklama: A rasul is a prophet given a new law or a special mission to convey a message that renews previous rulings. Every rasul is also a nabi.

sorular.soru: What is the fundamental difference between a nabi and a rasul?
secenekler: A) A nabi is superior, while a rasul is lower in rank
B) There is no difference between them
C) A nabi does not bring a new law; a rasul is sent with a new law or a special mission to convey a message
D) A nabi is sent only to Muslims
sorular.aciklama: A nabi is a prophet who receives revelation but does not bring a new law. A rasul is described as a prophet sent with a new law or a special mission to convey a message.

sorular.soru: How many prophets are named in the Quran?
sorular.aciklama: Twenty-five prophets are named in the Quran.

sorular.soru: What can be understood from the statement, "Every rasul is also a nabi, but not every nabi is a rasul"?
secenekler: A) There are more rasuls than nabis
B) There are more nabis than rasuls
C) There are equal numbers of both
D) A rasul is of a lower rank
sorular.aciklama: This statement means that every rasul is a prophet, but not every prophet is called a rasul. Therefore, there are more nabis than rasuls.

sorular.soru: Will a new prophet come after Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
secenekler: A) Yes, a new prophet will come near the Day of Judgment
B) No, Muhammad (peace be upon him) is the last prophet
C) Jesus (peace be upon him) will come as a new prophet
D) There is no certain knowledge on this matter
sorular.aciklama: Muhammad ﷺ is the last prophet; no new prophet will come after him. The descent of Jesus (peace be upon him) does not mean a new prophethood. (al-Ahzab 33:40)

sorular.soru: When does life in the grave begin?
secenekler: A) After the Day of Judgment
C) At the place of gathering
D) Before life in this world
sorular.aciklama: Life in the grave is the period of barzakh (transition) that begins immediately after a person dies and lasts until the Day of Judgment.

sorular.soru: What does mahshar (place of gathering) mean?
secenekler: A) The inside of the grave
B) The place where all people will be gathered for judgment after the Day of Judgment
sorular.aciklama: Mahshar is the great place of gathering where all people will be brought together to give an account after the Day of Judgment.

sorular.soru: What does mizan (divine measure or scale) mean?
secenekler: B) The punishment of the grave
C) The divine measure or scale on which deeds will be weighed
sorular.aciklama: Mizan refers to the divine measure or scale on which good and bad deeds will be weighed in the Hereafter.

sorular.soru: What does Sirat (the bridge of the Hereafter) mean?
secenekler: C) The questioning in the grave
D) The scale in the Hereafter
sorular.aciklama: Sirat is the bridge of the Hereafter that is said to be set over Hell. This is a matter of the unseen; its details are known only to the extent that Allah has made them known.

sorular.soru: Which questions are asked during the questioning in the grave?
secenekler: A) "How many years did you live? What work did you do?"
B) "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?"
C) "How many prayers did you perform? How many fasts did you observe?"
sorular.aciklama: During the questioning in the grave, the angels Munkar and Nakir ask three questions: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?"

sorular.soru: Who receives the blessings and punishment of the grave?
secenekler: A) Both are given equally to everyone
B) Blessings are given to those who lived with iman, and punishment to those who died in disbelief and hypocrisy
C) There is only punishment, with no blessing
D) There is only blessing, with no punishment
sorular.aciklama: The blessings of the grave are described as being for those who lived with iman, while the punishment of the grave is described as being for those who died in disbelief and hypocrisy. The final judgment concerning sinful believers rests with Allah's mercy and justice.

sorular.soru: What kind of sign of the Day of Judgment is the Dajjal?
secenekler: C) It is not a sign
sorular.aciklama: The Dajjal is described as a lying and deceptive figure who is said to cause great tribulation near the Day of Judgment. His appearance is one of the major signs.

sorular.soru: What is narrated about Jesus (peace be upon him) near the Day of Judgment?
secenekler: A) He will be sent again as a prophet
B) He will descend to earth and act according to the rulings of Islam
C) He will be judged in the Hereafter
D) It is narrated that he will bring a second Gospel
sorular.aciklama: It is narrated that Jesus (peace be upon him) will descend to earth near the Day of Judgment and act according to the rulings of Islam. This is not a new prophethood.

sorular.soru: What does barzakh (period of transition) mean?
secenekler: A) The region between Paradise and Hell
B) The period of transition between death and the Day of Judgment (life in the grave)
C) The name of the place of gathering
D) The edge of the bridge of Sirat
sorular.aciklama: Barzakh is the name given to the period of transition from death until the Day of Judgment. For this reason, life in the grave is also known as life in barzakh.

sorular.soru: What kind of sign of the Day of Judgment are Gog and Magog?
secenekler: C) They are not a sign
D) They are connected with the Night of Decree
sorular.aciklama: Gog and Magog are described as great groups of corrupters who are said to appear near the Day of Judgment. Their appearance is one of the major signs. (al-Anbiya 21:96)

sorular.soru: What does qadar mean?
secenekler: A) The period before Allah's creation
B) Allah's eternal knowledge and decree of all things
C) The choices a person makes through their own free will
D) Events that happen by chance
sorular.aciklama: Qadar is Allah's knowing, determining and recording all things eternally, through His knowledge that has no beginning.

sorular.soru: What does qada mean?
secenekler: A) The punishment for a sin
B) The occurrence of what Allah has decreed when its time comes
D) A person's power to change their destiny
sorular.aciklama: Qada is the creation and occurrence, when their time comes, of the things Allah decreed in eternity.

sorular.soru: According to the hadith of Jibril, how is belief in divine decree defined?
secenekler: A) "Believing that only good things come from Allah"
B) "Believing in divine decree, both its good and its evil"
C) "Believing that only death is in Allah's hands"
D) "Believing that divine decree can be changed"
sorular.aciklama: In the hadith of Jibril, belief in divine decree is defined as "believing in divine decree, both its good and its evil." This means that events that appear both good and difficult are within Allah's knowledge and decree.

sorular.soru: Which statement about belief in divine decree is correct?
secenekler: A) Divine decree frees people from all responsibility
B) Belief in divine decree does not eliminate human free will or responsibility
C) A person who believes in divine decree does not have to worship
D) Bad events are outside divine decree
sorular.aciklama: Belief in divine decree does not eliminate human free will or responsibility. People are responsible for their choices; everything is within Allah's eternal knowledge and decree.

sorular.soru: According to belief in divine decree, which statement about "good and evil" is correct?
secenekler: A) Good comes from Allah, and evil comes from humans
B) Both good and evil occur through Allah's creation
C) Evil does not come from Allah; Satan creates it
D) Humans create evil entirely by themselves
sorular.aciklama: According to Sunni belief, both good and evil occur through Allah's creation; humans are responsible for their own choices and actions.

sorular.soru: What is the main difference between the five pillars of Islam and the six articles of iman?
secenekler: B) The articles of iman concern actions, while the pillars of Islam concern the heart
C) The articles of iman are beliefs of the heart, while the pillars of Islam are acts of worship
D) Both consist only of outward acts of worship
sorular.aciklama: The six articles of iman (Allah, angels, books, prophets, the Hereafter, and divine decree) are beliefs of the heart; the five pillars of Islam (the shahada, salah, sawm, zakat, and Hajj) are acts of worship.

sorular.soru: Which of the six articles of iman concerns the Day of Resurrection and life after death?
secenekler: C) Belief in the Last Day
sorular.aciklama: Belief in the Last Day includes life after death, the Day of Resurrection, the gathering place, the divine scale, the bridge of the Hereafter, and Paradise and Hell.

sorular.soru: Of the four major revealed books, which is the only one Allah has said He will protect?
sorular.aciklama: "Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder (the Quran), and We will surely protect it." (al-Hijr 15:9) The Quran is the only book that Allah Himself has undertaken to protect.
